code_evidence.summary: AI-assisted token persistence saved Garmin refresh tokens with ordinary file-system defaults. On a shared host, a typical umask made the directory searchable and the token file world-readable; version 0.3.5 switched both paths to owner-only access.
code_evidence.mechanism: Client.dump serialized the DI refresh token, then used mkdir and write_text without permission modes; the release fix enforces directory mode 0o700, file mode 0o600, and no-follow creation.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: Native DI OAuth support introduced a JSON token store but left its directory and file permissions to the process umask.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The 0.3.5 release-line fix creates and tightens owner-only paths and rejects a pre-planted symlink during file creation.

candidate_hunks.code:
@@ -0,0 +642,23 @@ selected from new garminconnect/client.py
+    def dumps(self) -> str:
+        """Serialize session state to JSON string."""
+        data: dict[str, Any] = {
+            "di_token": self.di_token,
+            "di_refresh_token": self.di_refresh_token,
+            "di_client_id": self.di_client_id,
+            "it_token": self.it_token,
+            "it_refresh_token": self.it_refresh_token,
+            "it_client_id": self.it_client_id,
+            # JWT_WEB fields
+            "jwt_web": self.jwt_web,
+            "csrf_token": self.csrf_token,
+            "cookies": {c.name: c.value for c in self.cs.cookies.jar},
+        }
+        return json.dumps(data)
+
+    def dump(self, path: str) -> None:
+        """Write tokens safely to disk."""
+        p = Path(path).expanduser()
+        if p.is_dir() or not p.name.endswith(".json"):
+            p = p / "garmin_tokens.json"
+        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        p.write_text(self.dumps())
candidate_hunks.annotation: The new serializer places the long-lived DI refresh token in the JSON payload, then dump() creates its directory and file without explicit modes. Under a common umask of 022, other local accounts can traverse the directory and read the credential.

fix_hunks.code:
@@ -1191,12 +1192,33 @@ class Client:
         return json.dumps(data)
 
     def dump(self, path: str) -> None:
-        """Write tokens safely to disk."""
+        """Write tokens safely to disk with owner-only permissions.
+
+        The token file contains the DI refresh token, which grants persistent
+        account access. It is written as 0o600 inside a 0o700 directory so a
+        permissive process umask can't leave it world-readable on a shared host
+        (GHSA-wjhr-76vg-2hvc).
+        """
         p = Path(path).expanduser()
         if p.is_dir() or not p.name.endswith(".json"):
             p = p / "garmin_tokens.json"
-        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
-        p.write_text(self.dumps())
+        p.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # mkdir's mode is subject to umask and a no-op if the dir already
+        # exists; chmod enforces 0o700 unconditionally.
+        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
+            p.parent.chmod(0o700)
+        # Open with O_CREAT mode 0o600 (and O_NOFOLLOW where available so a
+        # pre-planted symlink can't redirect the write) instead of write_text,
+        # which would create the file under the umask first.
+        flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC
+        if hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW"):
+            flags |= os.O_NOFOLLOW
+        fd = os.open(p, flags, 0o600)
+        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as token_file:
+            token_file.write(self.dumps())
+        # Enforce 0o600 even if the file pre-existed with looser permissions.
+        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
+            p.chmod(0o600)
 
     def load(self, path: str) -> None:
         try:
fix_hunks.annotation: The release fix replaces the umask-dependent write with an owner-only directory, an O_NOFOLLOW file descriptor created as 0o600, and final chmod calls that also repair loose permissions on pre-existing paths.
